question:
Study the table below showing the maximum temperature (in °C) of five cities over six months, and answer the question.

City | Jan | Feb | Mar | Apr | May | Jun
Delhi | 21 | 24 | 30 | 36 | 40 | 38
Mumbai | 29 | 30 | 32 | 33 | 34 | 33
Kolkata | 26 | 28 | 33 | 36 | 37 | 35
Chennai | 29 | 30 | 32 | 34 | 37 | 38
Shimla | 10 | 12 | 16 | 21 | 25 | 24

Q. What is the ratio of the total maximum temperature of Delhi across all six months to that of Shimla across all six months?
explanation: Total for Delhi = 21 + 24 + 30 + 36 + 40 + 38 = 189. Total for Shimla = 10 + 12 + 16 + 21 + 25 + 24 = 108. The ratio is 189 : 108, which simplifies by dividing by 27 to 7 : 4. Option B (4 : 7) inverts the numerator and denominator.

शहर | जन | फ़र | मार्च | अप्रैल | मई | जून
दिल्ली | 21 | 24 | 30 | 36 | 40 | 38
मुंबई | 29 | 30 | 32 | 33 | 34 | 33
कोलकाता | 26 | 28 | 33 | 36 | 37 | 35
चेन्नई | 29 | 30 | 32 | 34 | 37 | 38
शिमला | 10 | 12 | 16 | 21 | 25 | 24

प्र. सभी छह महीनों में दिल्ली के कुल अधिकतम तापमान का शिमला के कुल अधिकतम तापमान से अनुपात क्या है?
explanation_hi: दिल्ली का कुल योग = 189 और शिमला का कुल योग = 108 है। 27 से विभाजित करने पर अनुपात 7 : 4 प्राप्त होता है। विकल्प B गलत है क्योंकि यह व्युत्क्रम अनुपात है।

question:
Study the table below showing the maximum temperature (in °C) of five cities over six months, and answer the question.

City | Jan | Feb | Mar | Apr | May | Jun
Delhi | 21 | 24 | 30 | 36 | 40 | 38
Mumbai | 29 | 30 | 32 | 33 | 34 | 33
Kolkata | 26 | 28 | 33 | 36 | 37 | 35
Chennai | 29 | 30 | 32 | 34 | 37 | 38
Shimla | 10 | 12 | 16 | 21 | 25 | 24

Q. In which month was the average maximum temperature across all five cities the highest?
explanation: Sum of temperatures for each month across all 5 cities: Jan = 21+29+26+29+10 = 115; Feb = 24+30+28+30+12 = 124; Mar = 30+32+33+32+16 = 143; Apr = 36+33+36+34+21 = 160; May = 40+34+37+37+25 = 173; Jun = 38+33+35+38+24 = 168. May has the highest sum (173), hence the highest average. Option C (June) is wrong as its sum is 168.

question:

Year | AC First | AC Tier-2 | AC Tier-3 | Sleeper | General
2019 | 45 | 120 | 310 | 850 | 1200
2020 | 30 | 80 | 220 | 600 | 800
2021 | 35 | 95 | 260 | 700 | 950
2022 | 50 | 140 | 350 | 900 | 1300
2023 | 60 | 160 | 400 | 1000 | 1500

Q. In the year 2022, what percentage of the total passengers traveled in AC classes combined (AC First, AC Tier-2, and AC Tier-3)?
explanation: In 2022, total AC passengers = 50 (First) + 140 (Tier-2) + 350 (Tier-3) = 540. Total passengers across all classes in 2022 = 50 + 140 + 350 + 900 + 1300 = 2740. The percentage is (540 / 2740) × 100 ≈ 19.71%. Option B (18.50%) is incorrect.

question:

Year | Tea Exports | Coffee Exports
2018 | 300 | 150
2019 | 320 | 180
2020 | 280 | 160
2021 | 350 | 210
2022 | 360 | 240
2023 | 400 | 250

Q. Which of the following statements is NOT correct regarding the given export data?
answer: B) Coffee exports continuously increased every single year from 2018 to 2023.
options: A) Tea exports were highest in the year 2023.
B) Coffee exports continuously increased every single year from 2018 to 2023.
C) Total combined exports of tea and coffee exceeded 600 thousand tonnes in 2023.
D) Tea exports in 2020 were lower than tea exports in 2019.
explanation: Coffee exports dropped from 180 in 2019 to 160 in 2020, so they did NOT continuously increase every single year. Thus statement B is false, making it the correct answer for a NOT correct question.
